PullRequest.Title: Remove wall-clock throttle from PromptInputModel sync
PullRequest.Body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/339672

- Remove `@throttle(0)` from [`PromptInputModel._sync`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f770144247addc066b9e5cb34fa96f4a5fe74ae6/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/capabilities/commandDetection/promptInputModel.ts#L273-L280), so each xterm write, cursor move, or data event syncs the model immediately.
- [`throttle`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f770144247addc066b9e5cb34fa96f4a5fe74ae6/src/vs/base/common/decorators.ts#L113-L126) compares against `Date.now()`, which moves backwards when the system clock is adjusted. On Windows, Chromium also [periodically resyncs its wall clock to the system time](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/fcfd8f37188d64b88c6cb509009d8fc78a736eda/base/time/time_win.cc#L205-L219). After a backwards step, `throttle(0)` deferred the sync until the wall clock caught up, leaving the model on its previous value.
- That is the flaky Fish ghost text failure: the test asserts after a single `timeout(0)`, so a deferred sync left it reading `find . -name|`. Outside tests, the prompt input model stalled for as long as the clock moved back.
- Keep normal behavior unchanged: on a non-decreasing clock `throttle(0)` never defers, because the next allowed run time is the last run time.
- Leave the shared `throttle` decorator as it is.
- Add a test that moves only `Date` back between two writes.

Testing:

- Bundled this branch's `promptInputModel.test.ts` and `decorators.test.ts` and ran them in Node with the repo's mocha 10.8.2 and sinon 12.0.1: 50 passing, 1 pending. With main's `PromptInputModel`, the new test fails with `'foo|' !== 'foo bar|'`.
- Replaying the Fish ghost text test with `Date.now()` stepped back 5 ms or 16 ms between the second and third writes reproduced the CI failure 199/200 times on main and 0/200 times on this branch.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Faking only `Date` with `useFakeTimers({ now, toFake: ['Date'] })` follows [`codexSkuTelemetry.test.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f770144247addc066b9e5cb34fa96f4a5fe74ae6/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexSkuTelemetry.test.ts#L447).
- The test shape follows the neighboring [`should clear value when command finishes`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f770144247addc066b9e5cb34fa96f4a5fe74ae6/src/vs/platform/terminal/test/common/capabilities/commandDetection/promptInputModel.test.ts#L147-L160) test.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing, editing, or receiving echoed input at a shell prompt with command detection active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each xterm onData/onCursorMove/onWriteParsed event synchronously enters PromptInputModel._sync, scans the relevant local xterm buffer lines and cells, and emits onDidChangeInput only when value/cursor/ghost text changed. This scan must complete before prompt-model consumers observe the new state; asynchronous completion-provider results are downstream and not required for the model update itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Terminal process output/input is delivered through the existing pty/xterm pipeline and surfaces as parsed write, cursor, and data events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more local xterm events per pty write/input chunk; Event.any does not itself coalesce them, while unchanged reconstructed state suppresses downstream model-change events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same xterm events and pty boundary drove _sync before the diff. With a nondecreasing clock, throttle(0) invoked _sync immediately on every event, including multiple events in the same millisecond.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The upstream pty delivery precedes the synchronous local model scan; no new IPC call is made by _sync.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: When terminal suggestions are enabled and a prompt change meets quick-suggestion or trigger-character rules, enabled completion providers may be invoked, including extension-host providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request initiated by each effective prompt-state change, fan-out across enabled providers; duplicate xterm events with unchanged model state do not request completions, and newer requests cancel the prior token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same prompt changes initiated the same provider requests before the diff whenever the wall clock was nondecreasing; the removed zero-delay throttle provided no normal-path batching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider work is asynchronous and off the prompt-model update critical path, though request initiation occurs from the synchronous change listener.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU work scales with the number and width of command lines between the command-start marker and cursor, visible rows below the cursor, and cells inspected for ghost text. Event frequency follows xterm write/cursor/data events, but duplicate triggers that produce identical state do not fan out onDidChangeInput.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Buffer reconstruction and local listeners run synchronously and serially on the renderer/UI thread. Optional completion providers fan out asynchronously across enabled providers; a newer request cancels the prior token, although provider implementations determine how promptly cancellation stops boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache for buffer reconstruction. State comparison suppresses downstream events for unchanged results. Completion requests keep current prompt state and cancel the prior token; no new cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High. The decorator implementation compares lastRun + 0 with Date.now using <=, so every call runs immediately for equal or increasing timestamps. The removed wrapper only changes behavior after a backward wall-clock step.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact command length, row count, xterm event multiplicity, and enabled completion-provider count vary, but the before/after call cardinality is established for normal clocks: it is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The synchronous scan is a pre-existing hot-path cost, and removing throttle(0) does not increase its normal-path frequency or downstream fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continuing to type or receive prompt updates after the system wall clock moves backward
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed code immediately performs the same synchronous xterm-buffer reconstruction and state notification used during ordinary input. Before the diff, throttle(0) scheduled a timer for the wall-clock gap and suppressed subsequent calls behind its pending flag, so prompt-model progress waited for the clock to catch up.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing pty/xterm events deliver shell echo and parsed terminal writes that trigger local prompt reconstruction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more trigger events per write/input chunk; during clock rollback the diff restores immediate handling for each event, while unchanged-state checks bound downstream notifications to effective state changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After a backward clock step, the first call created a timer for the rollback gap and the pending flag suppressed subsequent sync calls. This was the stale-model failure the change removes; outside rollback, behavior was already immediate per event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The local synchronous scan now runs before each affected event returns instead of being deferred until the wall clock catches up.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: A restored prompt-state change can conditionally initiate existing terminal completion providers, including extension-host providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Conditional on suggest settings and input shape; one request per effective model change can fan out across enabled providers, with prior request tokens canceled on replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: During the erroneous rollback stall these requests were likewise delayed because no current prompt-state event was emitted; under ordinary clocks the same requests already occurred at the same effective input cadence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Request initiation follows model notification, while provider completion is asynchronous and not required for prompt-model progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: During the rollback interval, work now scales normally with effective xterm input changes and command/viewport size rather than collapsing all changes into one delayed scan. Downstream model-change events occur only for distinct reconstructed states.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model scans remain synchronous and serialized. Optional completion requests can overlap only according to existing provider cancellation behavior; the diff restores the same scheduling used before and after the rollback interval under ordinary clock progression.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No buffer cache is added or removed. State equality still suppresses duplicate notifications. Optional suggestion requests retain their existing cancellation behavior; there is no new persistent or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High. The decorator's pending branch and wall-clock arithmetic directly explain the rollback-only difference, and the new test exercises that path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backward clock adjustments are uncommon and their duration varies. High-throughput writes while the model remains in PromptInputState.Input could perform more immediate CPU work than the stalled pre-diff state, but this is restoration of established normal behavior rather than a new multiplicity or unbounded mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The extra rollback-interval work is required to eliminate a correctness-only stale-model stall and matches the existing non-rollback scheduling; retaining the accidental suppression would reintroduce the bug.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced prompt synchronization through xterm events, buffer reconstruction, UI listeners, and optional completion-provider boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found. The removed zero-delay wall-clock throttle was not a coalescer on normal clocks; it only suppressed work after backward clock movement. The PR fixes stale state rather than a qualifying shipped performance regression, so no regression-fix record was submitted.
